binders: An arbitrary finite index type iota.
An arbitrary sample type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A probability measure mu on Omega.
A family B = (B_i) indexed by iota, with each B_i a function from Omega to Bool.
Arbitrary real numbers lambda and t.
hypotheses: The Boolean-valued functions B_i are mutually independent under mu.
For every index i, B_i is measurable into Bool with its discrete (top) measurable space.
The real parameter lambda is strictly positive.
conclusions: Let X_i(omega) be 1 if B_i(omega) is true and 0 otherwise, and let S(omega) = sum over all i of X_i(omega). Then mu({omega : S(omega) >= t}), represented as a real number, is at most exp(-lambda*t) times the product over all i of the integral with respect to mu of exp(lambda*X_i(omega)).
mathematical_definitions: X_i(omega) := 1_{B_i(omega) = true}, viewed as a real-valued 0-1 indicator.
The left side is (mu({omega : t <= S(omega)})).toReal; because mu is a probability measure, it is the ordinary real probability of that event.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite mutually independent family of measurable Boolean random variables on a probability space, every positive real lambda, and every real threshold t, the probability that the number of true variables is at least t is bounded above by exp(-lambda*t) multiplied by the product of the individual exponential moments E_mu[exp(lambda X_i)], where X_i is the 0-1 indicator that B_i is true.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be finite, although it may be empty.
The random variables are specifically Boolean-valued and enter the bound only through their real 0-1 indicators.
Mutual independence and individual measurability are explicit premises; identical distribution is not assumed.
The measure is required to be a probability measure.
Lambda must be strictly positive, while the threshold t is completely unrestricted and may be negative or nonintegral.
For an empty index type the sum is 0 and the product is 1; the resulting statement remains nonvacuously well-defined.
The left side uses toReal on the event measure, but the probability-measure assumption guarantees finiteness, so this does not create an infinite-measure collapse.

The exponential-moment integrands take only the finite values 1 and exp(lambda), so under a probability measure their Bochner integrals are finite; the library's fallback behavior for nonintegrable functions does not affect this proposition.
No inconsistent or impossible premise is apparent from the dossier.
ambiguities: The one-level body shown for indexed independence delegates to a kernel-level independence predicate whose internal definition is outside the dossier; the exposed interface supports the standard interpretation of mutual independence, but not a further low-level reconstruction.

The displayed implementation body of the integral is opaque at this boundary, although its type and surrounding normed-space instances identify the standard real-valued Bochner integral, and the bounded measurable integrands make convention edge cases immaterial.
